---
title: "Building from source"
description: "One CMake tree, two artifacts: the Linux .so and the Windows .dll."
---

One source tree produces both drop-in artifacts. The build is plain CMake (≥ 3.16), pinned to
**C++11 with no compiler extensions** — that floor is deliberate, so the library builds and runs
beside the old toolchains EOS-era games actually shipped with.

## Linux `.so` (for native Linux games)

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target eos_shared --parallel
# -> build/libEOSSDK-Linux-Shipping.so
```

## Windows `.dll` (for Windows games, including under Proton/Wine)

Cross-compiled from Linux with MinGW-w64:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-win -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/toolchain-mingw-w64.cmake
cmake --build build-win --target eos_shared --parallel
# -> build-win/EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll
```

You'll need `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++` (package `mingw-w64` on most distros). The
[toolchain file](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined/blob/main/cmake/toolchain-mingw-w64.cmake)
links the runtime **statically**, so the resulting DLL needs no MinGW runtime DLLs shipped
alongside it. If Wine is installed, the cross-built test binaries run under it automatically.

Building natively on Windows with MSVC also works — configure with no toolchain file and build
the `eos_shared` target (the DLL lands under the configuration subdirectory, e.g.
`build/Release/EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll`).

## Targets and layout

| Target | What it is |
|---|---|
| `eos_shared` | The drop-in shared library (named exactly like Epic's artifact per platform). |
| `eosr_core` | Static library with the whole portable implementation; the flat C ABI in `src/flat/` is a thin layer over it. |
| `unit_tests`, `integration_tests`, `integration_trace` | The test suites (built when `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, the default). |

Dependencies are deliberately tiny and vendored: [Monocypher 4.0.3](https://monocypher.org/)
(X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 for the authenticated mesh) ships in `third_party/`, and the
header-only test framework `doctest` is compiled into test binaries only. There is nothing to
`apt install` beyond a compiler and CMake.

## Running the tests

```sh
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure        # native Linux
ctest --test-dir build-win --output-on-failure    # cross build, runs under Wine
```

The suite has five tiers:

- **`unit_tests`** — hundreds of cases over the core: crypto known-answer tests, Noise XX against
  the published vectors, config resolution, identity slots, every interface's behavior.
- **`integration_tests`** — loads the *real built* `.so`/`.dll` through the C ABI exactly like a
  game would, including ABI out-parameter contracts.
- **`integration_trace`** — drives a full SDK lifetime with tracing enabled and asserts on the
  files written.
- **`abi_mesh_probe`** — two real processes, each loading the built artifact, meshing over
  loopback: authenticated discovery, Friends/UserInfo, Sessions search/join, and P2P payload
  delivery proven end to end.
- **`export_surface`** — verifies the built library exports `EOS_*` symbols and *nothing else*
  (Unix; the Linux link also pins this with a version script).

[`scripts/test-all.sh`](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined/blob/main/scripts/test-all.sh)
builds and tests both targets in one go, skipping the Windows half politely
if MinGW or Wine is missing. For memory checking, configure a separate build directory with
`-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address,undefined"` — the suite is expected to run clean under
ASan + UBSan.

## Continuous integration

The repository has a manual CI workflow (**Actions → CI → Run workflow**) that builds the matrix —
native Linux, MinGW-w64 cross + Wine, and native MSVC — runs the full test suite on each, and
uploads both shipping artifacts. A sanitizer job runs the leak-clean tests under ASan + UBSan and
the loaded-library tiers with their documented process-lifetime globals excluded from leak checks.
It runs on demand rather than on every push, by design.

Alpha releases use a separate manual workflow (**Actions → Release alpha → Run workflow**), available
after the workflow is on `main`. It accepts only `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-alpha.NUMBER` tags and only runs
from `main`. Every release rebuilds and retests Linux, MinGW/Wine, native MSVC, and the sanitizer
gate; verifies the exact version and commit written to `runtime.json`; creates deterministic Linux
and Windows archives with embedded hashes; then verifies those archives before anything can be
published. Leave `publish` off for a release-candidate rehearsal. If that succeeds, rerun the same
version from the same `main` commit with `publish` on to create the GitHub prerelease. An existing tag
or release is refused rather than overwritten.

The [wiki you are reading](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined/tree/main/wiki) deploys
from its own manual workflow.
